podcast.title: Band's Future Uncertainty (Pre-2017 Album)
podcast.body: For several years, the band was not fully inactive but had somewhat receded, with members engaging in parallel projects such as Iggy Pop's album and Eagles of Death Metal (inferred from "Iguos Ordes Metal"), causing uncertainty among fans about the band's future direction. "la banda no estaba ni inactivo pero sí que se había quedado un poco de lado, habían salido esos proyectos paralelos como de Iguos, Ordes Metal, teníamos ese disco con Iguipop, entonces unos ya no sabían poco cuál iba a ser el futuro de la banda."

podcast.title: Absence of Grand Collaborations
podcast.body: The band's 2017 album is noted for not featuring the extensive and "grand" collaborations that Queen of the Stone Age has historically been accustomed to, which was a defining characteristic of some of their previous works. "tampoco tienes esas grandísimas colaboraciones a las que estamos acostumbrados en la banda."

srcs.episode: Queens of The Stone Age  - Villains (información y reseña)

podcast.title: Career Longevity and Rock's State
podcast.body: With a career spanning over 20 years, Queen of the Stone Age has been a significant force in rock music. The release of their 2017 album was met with a mix of apprehension and affection, given that rock as a genre is currently undergoing a period of evolution and is not at its peak, leading to questions about whether the band would retain its classic sounds from the mid-90s. "son más de 20 años de carrera, de lo mejor que hemos tenido en el rock, han pasado muchos años, el rock ahora mismo no está pasando con su mejor momento, todo parece que está evolucionando algo."

srcs.episode: Queens of The Stone Age  - Villains (información y reseña)

podcast.title: Enduring Appeal
podcast.body: The band's 2017 album is expected to please a wide audience, including long-time fans who will appreciate the maintained essence of Queen of the Stone Age and Josh Homme's updated sound, as well as newer 21st-century rock fans who might have found the band's earlier, harder sound too intense. "la esencia de Queen of the Stone Age se mantiene el sonido de Joe's Home se mantiene completamente firme pero a la vez son completamente actualizado y al mejor es a gente que era muy aficinada al rock del siglo XXI pero que se la hacía más duro el sonido del Queen of the Stone Age."

srcs.episode: Queens of The Stone Age  - Villains (información y reseña)

podcast.title: Evolution of Sound (Technical vs. Artistic)
podcast.body: The band's 2017 album shows a technical evolution in its sound, moving towards cleaner, drier, and slightly sharper tones, as opposed to an artistic revolution. This shift is noted by early critics using descriptors like "caramelized," "pompous," and "dry," reflecting a general trend in rock music rather than a unique band development. "el sonido ha evolucionado bastante, ya tenemos las primeras críticas del disco y todas hacen referencia conme evoluciona un poco el sonido de la banda no tanto artísticamente sino a nivel técnico y la verdad es que se están poniendo un montón de adjetivos un tanto raros como a Caramelado, pomposo, seco."

podcast.title: Expectation of Sound Evolution
podcast.body: Each new album released by Queen of the Stone Age generates significant discussion about its potential sound and the influences brought by its collaborators, a testament to their diverse and often changing musical partnerships. "cada vez que salen disco de los Queen of Stone Age nos preguntamos un poco a qué va a sonar y qué influencias va a tener de colaboraciones."

srcs.episode: Queens of The Stone Age  - Villains (información y reseña)

podcast.title: Fan Expectations and Past Sound
podcast.body: Die-hard fans of the band often yearn for the "fantastic era" of 'Rated R' and its associated chaotic sound (inferred from "de caos"), but this sound, despite its quality, is now considered somewhat outdated. After 20 years, expecting the band to revert to this older style is deemed unviable. "los más fans aferrimos, seguimos echando a lo mejor de menos esa etapa tan fantástica del rated art y de caos pero bueno han pasado ya muchos años es un sonido que ha quedado a pesar de su calidad relativamente desactualizado."

srcs.episode: Queens of The Stone Age  - Villains (información y reseña)

podcast.title: History of Notable Collaborators
podcast.body: Throughout its history, Queen of the Stone Age's projects have featured a roster of prominent rock musicians from the last 30 years, including PJ Harvey, Rob Halford of Judas Priest, Dave Grohl (inferred from "de Prolder"), members of The Breeders (inferred from "los buffiders"), original members of Kyuss (inferred from "Calleos"), and even a cameo from Shirley Manson of Garbage. "en el proyecto de los Queen of Stone Age ha pasado lo mejor de los últimos 30 años del rock, ha pasado Pierre Harvey, ha pasado Rob Halford de Judas Priest, ha pasado de Prolder, los buffiders, han pasado miembros originales de Calleos."

podcast.title: Prison Performance Incident
podcast.body: The band was kicked out of a prison while performing because officials found their song "Feel Good Hit of the Summer" to be inappropriate for the audience of inmates. "Queen of the Stone Age with a song that got them kicked out of a prison when they played it. Prison officials didn't think that was a very appropriate song to play for a bunch of comics."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Unstable Lineup and Collaborators
podcast.body: Apart from Josh Homme as the leader, the band's lineup is not particularly stable. Following Nick Oliveri's departure, the group largely revolved around Homme and a rotating cast of collaborators, leading to anticipation about the influences and contributions on each new release. "la formación de Queen of Stone Age no es especialmente estable aparte de Ios Home en Lidya y tras la marcha de Nico Livieri yo creo que el grupo se reduce a Ios Home con toda esa gente con la que se colabora."

xref.title: Josh Homme as Sole Member (Early 2004)
xref.body: In early 2004, following the firing of Nick Oliveri and the departure of Mark Lanegan, Josh Homme became the only remaining member of Queens of the Stone Age. He continued the band, given his primary role in writing 90% of the music and serving as the lead singer. "So this meant that in early 2004, Queen of the Stone Age was down to just one member, Josh Hommie."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Evolving Sound
xref.body: Queens of the Stone Age is known for taking chances and risks with each new record, actively avoiding repetition and embracing a "curve ball" approach to their sound. This commitment to change means fans never quite know what to expect, and the constantly shifting lineup contributes to this sonic evolution. "The last thing Josh Hommie and whatever his crew is in Queen of the Stone Age want to do is repeat themselves."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Music Video Director
xref.body: After his hit song, Liam Lynch went on to direct music videos for prominent bands such as Foo Fighters, Queens of the Stone Age, Eagles of Death Metal, Royal Blood, No Doubt, Weird Al, They Might Be Giants, and Tenacious D. "He went on to direct music videos for the Foo's, Queen of the Stone Age, Eagles of Death Metal, Royal Blood, No Doubt, Weird L. They might be giants in Tenacious D."
